Priority tiers

Apply first — Bengaluru strong fit

Best combination of Bengaluru seat evidence, direct GCC/product ownership, current or recent hiring signal, and fit to Pega + integrations + production ownership.

Companies: Commonwealth Bank, First Citizens India, Booking Holdings India, Empower, Cisco India, JPMorganChase, Nokia India, Broadridge, Societe Generale, BT Group

Apply selectively / referral-led

Good teams, but one constraint must be checked first: seniority, CDH-only specialization, Chennai/Pune center of gravity, rare openings, or team ambiguity.

Companies: Pegasystems India, Siemens, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, John Deere, VOIS, Sun Life, NatWest, Shell India, Intel India

Monitor / verify before spending energy

Bengaluru or Pega evidence exists, but current direct role evidence is thinner, global-only, older, operations/RPA-heavy, or not clearly your 4-year Pega band.

Companies: Wells Fargo, Standard Chartered, Carelon, Ameriprise, Telstra, GE HealthCare, Maersk, Capital One, Bosch, Levi Strauss, FNF, AXA, PayPal, Dell, Nike, Unilever

Bengaluru Top 50 · every Pega product/GCC team in one place · 2026-11-11

50 companies ranked by Bengaluru fit and evidence strength, with 308 named people (244 with public LinkedIn profiles). Each company shows what the team does, how it works, who to contact in what order, what to ask and the watch-outs. Companies below rank 30 have thin or negative Bengaluru evidence and are kept so you don't research them again.

Method and limits: Deep public lookup per team: site-restricted search results for public LinkedIn profile pages, official or mirrored job descriptions, Pega.com customer stories/PegaWorld sessions and public posts. Profile URLs are the public identity pages returned by search; no login, no crawling, no contact details. Project text is what each person publicly wrote about their own work, so it shows what the team does but not current reporting lines or vacancies. Priority: 1 = message first (near-peer, honest team reality), 2 = architect/lead (technical depth), 3 = manager (only with a role ID or after peer context), 4 = recruiter/TA (only with a live requisition).
Message rules: Keep connection notes under 300 characters. Name the workstream you read about, ask one specific question, and never ask a stranger for a referral in the first message. Contact managers only with a role ID; while a CBA interview is in progress, do not message its interviewers.

How the team works: Squads with a chapter model: chapter leads hold Pega craft standards across squads, managers own delivery. Most ICs are Senior Software Engineers (CSSA, often + CPDC/AWS). Hires come mainly from TCS, Capgemini, Sopra Steria, Deloitte, Coforge and Siemens; some seats are filled through staffing firms (e.g., Quess), so ask whether a role is direct.

Day to day: 40% office attendance per month (several 2025–2026 reviews); cab and shuttle provided; strong AI branding (#1 APAC bank in the Evident AI Index); graduate Launch Pad programme. Outreach blueprint · architecture fit, scripts, micro-dossiers, 7-day sprint · 2026-11-11

Built from the Bengaluru Top 50. Tiers group companies by architectural fit with your Kafka, replay/dead-letter, metadata-mapping and observability work.

Your positioning: Pega CSSA · event-driven Kafka integration · Service-REST replay & dead-letter recovery · metadata-driven JSON mapping · Pega observability
Proof points: Batch-to-real-time Kafka ingestion across 50+ topics, millions of records, seven APAC markets · Multi-hour batch runs cut to under 15 minutes · Service-REST replay + dead-letter recovery: incident recovery from ~2 hours to under 2 minutes · Runtime metadata-driven JSON mapping: new-format onboarding from ~4 weeks to ~10 minutes · $250K+ annual savings from automation (hub profile figure)
Stay honest: Production depth is integration, case management and observability. CDH strategy design is not production experience, so position for the data and integration side of decisioning teams.

Module 1 · Architecture alignment & GCC tiers

T1

High-Throughput & Event-Driven

Companies: Commonwealth Bank / ASB, Cisco India, First Citizens India, Wells Fargo India, JPMorganChase India, Goldman Sachs, BNY, Siemens, John Deere India, Booking Holdings India, MBRDI (benchmark)

Evidence: Job descriptions and talks name Kafka, events and async patterns (CBA/ASB JD), externalised Kafka on OpenShift (Cisco PegaWorld 2025), Kafka/JMS (First Citizens SE II JD), Kafka/async plus queue processors on WaaS 24.1.3 (Wells Fargo), payment investigations at SWIFT/Fed volume (Wells, Goldman, JPMC), sanctions screening (BNY), 8M+ invoices across 40+ countries (Siemens CCMT) and real-time agent data for ~10,000 agents (Booking).

Production friction points:

  • Consumer lag and backpressure when topic volume outpaces queue processors or data flows; node scaling is reactive.
  • Replays create duplicate cases or double writebacks because handlers are not idempotent.
  • Poison messages are handled by hand, so a bad payload turns into a multi-hour incident with log digging.
  • Schema drift across markets/versions breaks hard-coded mappings at every rollout.
  • No end-to-end trace from topic offset to case ID to downstream writeback, so support cannot prove where an event died.
  • Re-platforming (OpenShift, Pega Cloud, active-passive DR) changes rebalancing and failover behaviour of consumers.

Your talking points:

  • Throughput without fragility: I moved batch integrations to real-time Kafka ingestion across 50+ topics and seven markets. Multi-hour batch windows came down to under 15 minutes, and handlers are idempotent, so replays never create duplicate cases.
  • Recovery as a feature, not a runbook: I built Service-REST replay and dead-letter handling that parks failed events with case context and reprocesses them automatically. Incident recovery went from ~2 hours to under 2 minutes, with monitoring that ties offset → case → writeback.
T2

Decisioning & Intelligence

Companies: Commonwealth Bank (CDH / Next Best Conversation), Standard Chartered (Bengaluru CDH), NatWest Group, VOIS (Vodafone), HSBC, Verizon, Telstra India, Pegasystems India (CDH / Process AI engineering)

Evidence: Public sources: ~200 adaptive models at ~200 ms decisions (CBA), 1,800 NBA actions across 8 channels and a Pega Cloud migration started because of timeouts (NatWest), 10+ channels for 6.4M customers (VOIS), a Bengaluru decisioning-architect hiring wave in 2025–26 (Standard Chartered), Process AI in case management (Telstra), and CDH/ML product teams (Pegasystems).

Production friction points:

  • Real-time event ingestion into CDH (Kafka data sets, data flows) cannot keep up with decision SLAs, so NBA runs on stale context.
  • Response capture at volume: late or missing responses starve adaptive models.
  • Validating strategy changes at scale before production (one public post notes teams without BOE fall back on manual testing).
  • Cloud migration and upgrade stability: timeouts, long upgrade cycles, data-flow tuning.
  • Onboarding each new channel or data source needs mapping code and a release.

Your talking points:

  • The data path into decisioning: real-time NBA usually fails on ingestion, not strategy (late, malformed or duplicate events). I build high-throughput Kafka ingestion with dead-letter handling and lag monitoring, so decisions run on current context.
  • Configurable onboarding: my metadata-driven JSON mapping layer cut new-source onboarding from ~4 weeks to ~10 minutes. For a CDH team, new channels or attributes can be wired by configuration, without a release. I'd pair with your decisioning architects rather than claim strategy-design depth.
T3

Core Case Management & Enterprise Modernisation

Companies: Empower India, Daimler Truck India (DTICI), Nokia India, Broadridge India, Société Générale GSC, BT Group, Morgan Stanley, Sun Life, Ameriprise India, Shell India, Carelon, MUFG Global Service, ANZ, Ford (Bengaluru), Nike / Levi's / Intel / GE HealthCare / Unilever and other Tier-B/C teams

Evidence: Pega 24.x with Constellation and 24/7 production support (Empower), legacy rebuilt in 14 weeks on Blueprint/Pega Cloud (DTICI), order orchestration and DevOps (Nokia), Infinity + Constellation + GenAI JDs (Broadridge), migration/modernisation of banking apps (Société Générale), BT Business platform modernisation (BT), KYC/onboarding platforms (Morgan Stanley), on-prem 8.8 with FileNet (MUFG).

Production friction points:

  • Legacy retirement: mapping old system-of-record formats into Pega data models, with reconciliation done in spreadsheets.
  • Upgrades (8.x → 24/25) and Constellation re-platforming expose custom UI and guardrail debt.
  • Writeback to systems of record fails silently, leaving cases and SOR out of sync until a support ticket arrives.
  • Background processing (file listeners, job schedulers, BIX extracts) grows into long nightly runs and on-call load.
  • Contractor-heavy maintenance concentrates knowledge in vendors.

Your talking points:

  • Batch retirement during modernisation: I replaced file/batch integrations with Kafka and REST, taking multi-hour runs to under 15 minutes and removing a nightly support burden. It's the kind of change that makes a re-platformed app cheaper to run, not just newer.
  • Self-healing writebacks and configurable mapping: failed SOR updates land in a replay/dead-letter queue with case context and recover automatically (~2 hours → under 2 minutes), and metadata-driven mapping makes new legacy formats a configuration task (weeks → minutes).

Module 3 · Pre-outreach checklist

CheckWhat to confirm
1. Production stack breakdownList what coexists with Pega from JDs, PegaWorld talks and engineer profiles: messaging (Kafka/JMS), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP, Pega Cloud vs on-prem/OpenShift), databases (Oracle/Postgres), services (Spring Boot/Java), UI (Constellation vs UI-kit), DevOps (Deployment Manager, Jenkins, Azure DevOps). Fit check: does at least one item match your Kafka/REST/observability strengths?
2. The hookFind one dated, public change: a migration, upgrade, Blueprint/Constellation rebuild, cloud move, new squad or new manager. Use it as the first line of every message. No hook means no message yet.
3. Contact hierarchyPeer (same band, recent joiner) → architect/lead (one technical question) → manager only with a role ID → leadership only for roadmap questions. Never message two people on the same squad on the same day. If you are in an active interview loop, message peers only.
4. Technical interview prepDerive the three likeliest deep-dive questions from that firm's JD and workstreams (not hearsay): usually one integration/resilience design, one platform/version question (Cloud, Constellation, upgrade) and one domain case-design question. Prepare a 3-minute whiteboard answer for each.
5. Red flagsContractor or staffing-firm seats posing as direct roles, '24/7 support' or 'BAU' wording, title inflation through consulting titles, Pega being replaced by Java/low-code alternatives, frozen or removed postings, and the lead or decision-makers sitting in another city.

Module 4 · 7-day sprint (15 targets)

  • At most 15 invitations a day and about 50 for the week; LinkedIn caps weekly invitations and limits personalised notes on free accounts, so check your own limits first.
  • Free account with few notes left: send the invitation without a note to peers and send the scripted message after they accept. Save personalised notes for leads and managers.
  • One follow-up only, 5–7 days after acceptance. No follow-up to leadership.
  • Log every touch (date, person, company, script, response) in one tracker; never contact two people from the same squad on the same day.
  • Do not share MBRDI-internal architecture, data or client details; talk in patterns and outcomes.

Comment on two relevant posts (e.g., a PegaWorld/Cisco or Kafka topic).
Day 3 · Tier-3 peersInvite 10 peers: Empower (Divya Mohanraj, Nithin H N), DTICI (Sivakumar Annameti, Subiksha Ramachandran), Booking (Satish Varma Penmetsa, Vartika Tiwari), Nokia (Lavanya Bevara, Sirisha Pullagura), Broadridge (Sahaja Nayuni), Société Générale (Sudhir Sharma). Day 5 · Architect/lead layerOnly for companies where a peer replied: invite or message 5–6 leads with one technical question each (e.g., Deepak Shahi, Nanda Kumari K B, Vivek Kumar, Shailendra Mishra, Rimjhim Srivastava).
Day 6 · Managers with role IDsSend the Persona-2 script to managers whose role you applied for: Abhi Gummaraju (FCI), Ankit Punjarwar (Empower), Suresh Kathi (Broadridge), Abhimanu Bhardwaj (Nokia), Anish Kumar K P (Booking, only if a role ID exists). Team insider · how each Pega team works · 2026-11-10

For each team: how it is structured, what it actually builds, and what working there is like. Refreshed on 2026-11-10 for 12 employers that matter most to your search. Lens: About 4 years Pega, CSA + CSSA, Kafka/REST/SFTP integrations, auto-finance collections domain, Bengaluru preferred.

How to read this: Team-insider ledger: how each India Pega team is structured, who the visible people are, what they appear to build, and what working there is like. Built from search-index LinkedIn profile text (not live LinkedIn verification), public posts, employer postings and employee-review sites. Review ratings are self-selected and vary by team and manager; treat them as signals to ask about, not facts about the specific team you would join. No person was contacted.

Team by team

Hyderabad (largest), Bengaluru

Pegasystems India

How the team is structured: Product company, so the Pega 'team' is the product itself. The India GenAI Engineering org is led by Shyam Agarwal (Sr. Director, Hyderabad, Jan 2026, previously 16+ years leading India UI/Mobile/Integration/Robotics engineering) and Santosh Hegde (Director, ML & AI, Bengaluru, since Sep 2024). Under them sit Senior Principal engineers such as Md Azaz Ali and Krishna Rastogi (both 2026 moves into GenAI), with Principals and Software Engineers below. Separate Consulting and Client Success orgs deliver for customers from Hyderabad.

What they actually build: Pega's own agentic AI: Agentic Case Processing, RAG/knowledge search, agent-to-agent and MCP integrations, DocAI, the GenAI Assistant Service, generative-evaluation and guardrail frameworks, and agent orchestration in 'Pega Vibe'. The 2–4-year Software Engineer role builds these capabilities with Pega rules and works with ML engineers.

Key people and what they indicate

PersonRole / level signalWhat they appear to work onBest outreach use
Shyam AgarwalSr. Director, GenAI Engineering · HyderabadVisible India leader for GenAI engineering after long-running UI, mobile, integration and robotics leadership.Architecture/org context; ask what 2-4 year engineers actually own in GenAI squads.
Santosh HegdeDirector, ML & AI · BengaluruML/AI leadership signal for Pega's India AI engineering footprint.Understand AI/ML expectations before positioning your AI tooling story.
Md Azaz AliSenior Principal Engineer · GenAISenior technical IC signal around GenAI capability build-out.Technical discovery around agentic AI, guardrails and platform engineering depth.
Krishna RastogiSenior Principal Engineer · GenAIAnother senior IC move into GenAI; indicates the team is senior-heavy above normal Pega application development.Benchmark the engineering bar and what Pega-product coding differs from GCC implementation.
Mihir ChaddarwalaPrincipal recruiter routeRecruiting route seen in the retained product/AI dossier, not an engineering evidence source.Use only after identifying a live product/AI requisition.

What it's like day to day: Strong learning culture and AI focus; many reviewers describe a 9-to-5 rhythm. Free lunch and dinner reported. Hybrid with 3 office days and a strict 60% attendance rule (Blind, Jun 2026).

Ratings: AmbitionBox 3.6/5 (357 reviews; WLB 3.7, promotions 2.9). Glassdoor WLB 3.8. Blind 3.3 (WLB 3.9, management 2.9).

Watch-outs: Recurring complaints about favouritism and politics among long-tenured managers, slow promotions and occasional layoffs. Consulting roles report leave depending on client approval.

For you: The best band fit found (2–4 years, CSA + CSSA, Bengaluru). You would build the platform rather than use it, which is rare. Be honest that your GenAI work is tooling, not production LLM platforms.

Sources: AmbitionBox reviews · Blind reviews · Shyam Agarwal (index) · Md Azaz Ali (index) · GenAI SE posting

Bengaluru, Manyata Tech Park

Commonwealth Bank (CBA India)

How the team is structured: A Bengaluru Pega CoE of about 20 developers and QA, built from scratch since 2021 by Muniprakash Ganji (Senior Engineering Manager), with knowledge transferred from Sydney and a joint onshore–offshore model. Other Pega leaders: Gurushankar C N (Engineering Manager / Chapter Lead – Pega, Fraud & Scam, CLSA) and Resmi Raveendran (Manager – Pega). NEW: CBA India is building ASB's India engineering capability (REQ266311): squads embedded in ASB tribes and chapters holding the craft. The first Pega squad for ASB was posted on 14 Oct 2026: Engineering Manager REQ266820 plus Senior Software Engineers REQ266821 and REQ266822. CBA India is led by MD & CEO Shubha Iyer.

What they actually build: Customer Decision Hub decisioning: 620+ 'Next Best Conversations' delivered for retail banking; CBA's Customer Engagement Engine runs on Pega CDH with about 200 models and about 200 ms decisions. Also Pega CLM/KYC for Institutional Banking & Markets. The new ASB squad covers case management, integrations (APIs, events, async patterns) and Pega architecture. ASB's stated agenda is to scale Pega across decisioning, workflow, lending and financial crime; it is also setting up a Pega CoE in NZ and has Customer Service, KYC, lending and payments apps on Pega.

Key people and what they indicate

PersonRole / level signalWhat they appear to work onBest outreach use

Anjana ASenior Software Engineer · Bengaluru10+ year Pega profile with Trebla/Smart POS and AI-assisted development signals.Near-team engineering reality check; ask about day-to-day coding and internal tooling.

What it's like day to day: 40% office attendance per month (several 2025–2026 reviews); cab and shuttle provided; strong AI branding (#1 APAC bank in the Evident AI Index); graduate Launch Pad programme. Blind WLB 4.4.

Ratings: Blind 3.5 (21 reviews; WLB 4.4, management 3.0). Glassdoor WFH benefit 4.2. PrepNPlaced 2.69 across 973 reviews (career growth 2.21 lowest, salary 3.64 highest).

Watch-outs: Manyata is a long commute for many. No free meals. Some reviewers cite limited growth paths and leadership comparing itself to big tech. One engineer left after 7 months for Booking (Oct 2025).

Live rescrape · 9 November 2026

Fresh run of both local scanners plus manual checks of the role IDs this hub was tracking. Everything below this section is retained research from September–October; this section is the only part refreshed today. A listing being visible today is not a confirmed vacancy, salary band or approved experience exception.

What was run: the Career Desk scanner (job_runner.py --mode all, 408 targets) for LinkedIn public search, 377 employer career portals and the India job boards, and the standalone pega_job_hunter.py across 108 GCC/product employers. Coverage limit: LinkedIn's public job API returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) after roughly 170–225 requests in both passes, so 329–357 of 408 targets were deferred, not searched. Deferred means unknown, not "no openings". Career portals: 26 of 345 attempted pages returned Pega listings; 117 failed to load and 145 had no usable search box. The nightly scheduled task had been failing since the folder reorganisation because it pointed to the old path; it has been repointed to 01_pega_career_intelligence\JobChange\JobChange.

Research audit · 22 September 2026

All listed contacts across the three people directories have now been investigated, with duplicates reconciled and source-specific outcomes retained. Employer attribution, geography, certifications and movement inferences are separated from actual vacancy evidence.

Coverage and access: All 355 contact occurrences across the referral directory, contact overview and team dossiers have research outcomes. The inventory contained 322 identity keys; one duplicate was reconciled. The 270 previously unchecked keys were investigated, including 33 follow-up searches for ambiguous entries. Successful verification varies by person. Your revised outreach priorities

Evidence rules used in this audit

  • Public source read: the actual post/page was accessible and its relevant content was read. A historic post still does not certify current employment.
  • Index-supported: exact-profile URL and relevant professional text matched in search results. Crawl dates were unavailable; stale headlines, overlapping jobs and old tenures remain possible.
  • Mixed / limited / unresolved: conflicting fields, missing geography, incomplete identity evidence or no relevant result. Do not use as a verified referral.
  • Likes, comments, certifications and attendance at an event do not prove current hiring, reporting lines, direct payroll or net headcount growth.
  • A departure, promotion or intern conversion is not automatically a new externally available seat. Company-level awards are not team-quality scores.

Hidden profile-pattern insights normal browsing can miss

Added 30 September 2026 by mining all 330 audited profile rows for repeated skill, domain, geography and seniority patterns. These are hypothesis generators, not proof of open requisitions. The point is to notice where your resume pattern repeats quietly even when the company is not the loudest brand.

1 · HSBC/BT are stronger than the logo ranking shows

Profile text repeatedly clusters around Global Payment Investigations, Pega Cloud, integration and Bengaluru/Pune delivery. That is closer to your Kafka/REST/SQL + collections/case-management story than a generic “big bank” label suggests.

Hidden move: ask about Global Payment Investigations / payment exception workflows first, not generic Pega openings. Your safest pitch is “payments/collections workflow + integration reliability,” not “I want any Pega role.”

2 · Deere collections: closest work, mixed payroll

Abhiraj’s client-project profile gives detailed CSFS collections, telephony, OAuth and DeereAI proof-of-concept evidence close to your Mercedes-Benz Financial Services experience. His own post names Coforge as the employer behind that Deere assignment. Shailendra’s direct Deere Bengaluru engineering role is not proven to share that programme.

Hidden insight: target the workstream, not a presumed direct GCC headcount or guaranteed internal referral.

3 · Project descriptions beat job titles

Compare named deliverables: Narendhar’s BT Infinity 24.2 workflow work, Dharani’s Cisco API-triggered cases and upgrade, Rabi’s Ford SaaS migration, and Abhiraj’s Deere collections integrations. These reveal more about likely role content than VP/LSA titles or generic AI headlines.

Hidden move: separate direct employees from vendor-assigned engineers, and hands-on deliverables from training, posts and credentials. The source-linked dossier shows these distinctions without needing a conversation to establish the basics.

4 · Integration evidence is a better predictor than Pega title alone

Profiles mentioning Kafka, REST/SOAP, APIs, PDC, Splunk, deployment automation, OpenShift, Helm, AWS, CI/CD or staging/data connectors map better to your resume than pure CDH/decisioning or generic Pega certification profiles.

Hidden move: in searches and outreach, combine Pega + Kafka, Pega + REST, Pega + payment investigations, Pega + collections, and Pega + cloud platform. This will find better matches than searching “Pega developer” alone.

5 · Some famous names are noisy, not bad

JPMC, Standard Chartered, Booking, Morgan Stanley and Citi contain good signals, but many matching profiles are senior, stale, overseas, mixed-platform or old-client-project evidence. That means the company is not useless; it means the route must be role-ID-led.

Hidden move: for these firms, do not ask broad contacts for “any Pega openings.” Ask with an exact requisition, team phrase and experience band. Otherwise your outreach lands in the wrong internal channel.

6 · Timing signal supports two outreach waves

Profile start dates cluster around June–September, peaking in July, with a smaller January bump. Company-level timing is too thin, but profile movement suggests hiring loops for July starts often close in April–May.

Hidden move: maintain two pipelines: immediate role-ID applications now, and a second referral wave before April–May for July/August joins. Do not wait until the visible opening appears if you can warm up the right peer first.

What not to infer: a repeated skill pattern is not a vacancy, a profile start date is not an offer date, and a senior profile is not a recruiter. These insights are meant to improve search terms, referral route selection and interview positioning.

GCC engineering culture ranking · evidence-weighted research instrument

October 2026 ranking of public evidence for engineering autonomy, modernity, innovation visibility and attrition signals across the GCC/company universe. This section now carries both the engineering ranking and a separate unscored lifestyle ledger. Scores and ranks are frozen from the supplied research dataset.

Read this before using the ranking. The score measures how much defensible public evidence exists for a strong engineering environment — not a company's true quality. Measured correlation between score and raw evidence volume is 0.839, so a low score predominantly means thin public evidence, not a bad place to work. 55 of 89 companies have no measurable tenure data and are recorded as Unknown, not penalised. Only compare companies inside the same evidence-confidence tier. Glassdoor ratings and compensation were not used — no reliable programmatic source was available. No private profile data was accessed. Scores are a research instrument for prioritising outreach, not a verdict on any employer or a prediction about any vacancy.

Rubric explainer

P1 · Architectural autonomy · max 30 points

What earns points: India/GCC-based senior, lead or top-level Pega architecture authority and evidence of owning platform decisions.

What loses points: Delivery/support-only signals, or no defensible local architecture authority.

P2 · Modernity & integration · max 30 points

What earns points: Heavy integration/event-driven work, modern UI/application signals, and cloud/platform ownership.

What loses points: Support-only or narrowly dated implementation evidence without modern, integration or cloud signals.

P3 · Innovation visibility · max 20 points

What earns points: Conference, award, community, hackathon or build-in-public evidence connected to engineering work.

What loses points: This pillar has no negative floor in the supplied rubric; absent public visibility earns no points.

P4 · Attrition index · max 20 points

What earns points: Measured, settled tenure patterns where at least three parseable engineer tenures are available.

What loses points: Departure-driven short tenure; unmeasured tenure is recorded as Unknown rather than penalised.

Two documented corrections to the rubric as written: (a) rubric arithmetic: Spec's Pillar 2 itemised to 25 but was labelled Max 30, making the rubric total 95. A third +5 cloud/platform tier closes the gap to a true 100. (b) short-tenure rule: Low average tenure is penalised only where departure evidence outweighs join evidence; intern-conversion and new-team growth are not treated as burnout.

Lifestyle & total rewards · evidence ledger (not scored)

LIFESTYLE EVIDENCE LEDGER - deliberately NOT a score. Lifestyle perks vary by role, grade, shift and year, and sources openly contradict each other, so any numeric index would imply precision the evidence cannot support. Each claim therefore carries its own status and sources. Lifestyle claims are not scored on purpose. Perks vary by grade, shift and year, and sources openly contradict each other — the most widely repeated claim in this whole ledger, that Goldman Sachs Bengaluru gives free gourmet meals and free AC cabs, did not survive checking. Treat every CONTESTED_BY_ROLE and UNVERIFIED row as a question for the recruiter, not a fact. Ask specifically: is lunch free or subsidised, is transport all-day or late-hours only, how many days in office, and is parental insurance covered from day one without co-pay.

Low confidence — under-documented, NOT judged weak

A low score here reflects missing research coverage, not a weak engineering environment. Several companies in this tier are known-good targets whose evidence simply has not been gathered yet.

What each team is actually building · skills you need to get in

Based on the deep-dive scrape of what named people describe as their actual work — not their headline or certifications — this is a project-by-project breakdown of what skills the top candidates at each company are demonstrating. Learn these specific skills to match what they're doing, not just what their job title says.

The 5 Pega frameworks that dominate the hiring landscape

Framework / skill clusterWhat it actually isWhich companies use itHow to learn itYour current gap
Pega Smart Investigate (SIAA)Payment exception management. Three-tiered case model: Dispatch → Orchestration → Resolution. Handles SWIFT messages (MT/CBPRPlus XML), nostro/vostro reconciliation, FedService messages, email/fax. Auto-creates investigation cases from inbound payment exceptions. Built on top of CSFS. Now includes Agentic Automation with AI-driven resolution.Wells Fargo (Raja Reddy — expert), HSBC (Global Payment Investigations), Barclays (Harshad + Paridhi earned Smart Investigate badges Jul 2026), Lloyds Technology Centre (hiring specifically for this)Pega Academy: "Smart Investigate Agentic Automation" free modules. Study the 3-tier case architecture. Practice SWIFT message parsing concepts. The Pega Academy course covers dispatch cases, orchestration workflow, and resolution activities.Medium gap. You have case management + integration skills from collections. SWIFT messaging and nostro/vostro accounting are domain-specific — learn the vocabulary and case flow, your integration skills transfer directly.
Pega CSFS + CollectionsCustomer Service for Financial Services + Collections. Manages delinquent accounts through case lifecycle: grouping → contact strategies → payment plan negotiation → promise-to-pay evaluation. Uses CDH for Next-Best-Action on collection offers. File listeners for batch processing. Connects to telephony (CTI), email, IVR. Pega CSFS is the foundation layer that Smart Investigate and Smart Dispute sit on top of.John Deere Financial (Rahul Chaher built entire app on CSFS — collections/repossession/litigation/probate), Goldman Sachs (Pavan Kumar — Marcus Collections & Recoveries), Siemens (Anusha G — CCMT cash collection)Pega Academy: "Collections Operations Lifecycle" module (v3). Study the Manage Collections case type, file listener batch setup, payment plan scheduling. Your Mercedes-Benz collections experience maps almost 1:1 to this framework.Smallest gap. Your Mercedes-Benz Financial Services work IS this domain. Learn the Pega-specific framework terminology (Microjourneys, Manage Collections case type, CDH integration for NBA on collection offers). Rahul Chaher's project description reads like your resume.
Pega Smart Dispute (Issuer / Acquirer)Credit/debit card dispute management. Handles Visa Claims Resolution (VCR), Mastercom, Amex, ATM, and ACH disputes. Includes card scheme compliance rules, inbound/outbound processing, batch queues, duplicate scoring, dispute qualification scripts, VCR SOAP/REST connectivity, and accounting per Visa/MC guidelines. Two variants: Smart Dispute for Issuers and for Acquirers.Lloyds Technology Centre (hiring "Smart Dispute framework" expertise Jan 2025), NAB (Sarabdeep — Visa/MC disputes on Pega Smart Dispute), American Express (dispute/fraud modernization)Pega Academy: Smart Dispute modules. Study VCR message flow, dispute lifecycle stages, card scheme rules. Focus on how disputes integrate with payment networks — SOAP/REST connectors to Visa/MC.Medium gap. You haven't worked with card schemes directly, but the dispute case lifecycle and batch queue processing patterns are similar to collections. Integration skills (REST/SOAP) transfer well.
Constellation UI + DX APIPega's modern React-based UI framework. Replaces traditional harness/section-based UI with view-based approach. Uses client-side rendering (React), Redux state management. DX API (v2) separates data from layout. Supports "blended" mode (Constellation cases inside traditional portal) and "coexistence" mode. Theme Cosmos. Best practice: start new apps in Constellation, migrate existing gradually.Siemens (Renuka Deshpande — most prolific Constellation poster, Views expert), Booking (Saisindhu — Constellation + Theme Cosmos from day one; Navya — troubleshooting 25.1.2), Ford (Constellation bootcamp Jan 2026), CBA (Kavya — PegaInnovate 2026 Constellation exposure), Cisco (exploring)Pega Academy: "Discover Constellation" journey. Practice creating Constellation case types in App Studio. Study Views (not sections), Design Templates, responsive layouts. Build a small Constellation app. Key concept: understand blended UI migration strategy — most hiring teams are migrating, not greenfield.Medium gap. You have traditional UI experience. Constellation is React-based views, not harnesses/sections. Learn the view authoring in App Studio, understand the DX API differences (v1 vs v2), practice with the Pega Personal Edition.
Pega CDH / Decisioning / NBACustomer Decision Hub for Next-Best-Action. Adaptive models learn from interactions using contextual bandit algorithm. Engagement policies (eligibility, applicability, suitability). Channels, treatments, propensity scoring. Prediction Studio for model monitoring. Customer journeys influence NBA. Used for both marketing (NBA offers) and service (collections NBA). Requires CPDC certification.CBA (Manoj — Senior Decisioning Engineer, CDH/NBA), NAB (Customer Brain — 800 adaptive models), HSBC (Aditya Nath CLDA, Deepak Lama LDA), Standard Chartered (Vikas Soni CDH from HSBC), enGen (Sathya Prakash — CPDC + meetup on deployment)Pega Academy: CPDC certification path. Study Next-Best-Action Designer (5 steps: taxonomy, constraints, engagement policies, channels, analytics). Practice with Prediction Studio. Understand adaptive models and propensity scoring. This is a separate specialization from case management.Larger gap. CDH/Decisioning is a different domain from case management. You'd need CPDC certification and hands-on adaptive model experience. This is more of a long-term upskill than an immediate job entry strategy — unless a role explicitly says "CDH experience preferred but not mandatory."

Your skill priority list: what to learn in what order

Priority 1 — Already have, just need Pega-specific vocabulary

Collections/CSFS framework: Your Mercedes-Benz Financial work IS this. Learn the Pega-specific terms: Manage Collections case type, Microjourneys, file listener batch processing, CDH-linked payment plans, CTI/dialer integration. Target: John Deere, Goldman Sachs, Siemens CCMT.

Priority 2 — Low effort, high ROI

Constellation UI basics: Every company is migrating or planning to migrate. Learn Views (not sections), Design Templates, App Studio authoring, blended UI concept. You don't need to be an expert — just demonstrate you understand the migration path. Pega Academy "Discover Constellation" journey is free. Target: Siemens, Ford, Booking, CBA, Lloyds.

Priority 3 — Medium effort, differentiates you

Pega Smart Investigate / Smart Dispute: These are the two hottest banking frameworks. Smart Investigate = payment exceptions (Wells Fargo, HSBC, Barclays). Smart Dispute = card disputes (Lloyds, NAB, Amex). Study the case architecture, SWIFT message concepts, dispute lifecycle. You don't need to implement one — just understand the 3-tier case model and be able to discuss it intelligently. Target: Lloyds (actively hiring this), Wells Fargo, Barclays.

Priority 4 — Useful signal, not required

Kafka + OpenShift/Kubernetes basics: Cisco's migration and Sukan's CBA work both emphasize Kafka integration. Rabi's Ford work includes OpenShift. These aren't Pega-specific but show platform maturity. Create a Kafka Data Set in Pega Personal Edition, understand consumer/producer patterns. Get basic OpenShift/K8s concepts. Target: Cisco, CBA, Ford.

Priority 5 — Long-term investment

Pega GenAI awareness: Booking's hackathon, Sun Life's Knowledge Agent, Ford's CTO visit — GenAI is coming to every team. You don't need to build an LLM, but understand: GenAI Connect (bridges Pega to LLMs), Agentic Process Fabric (orchestrates AI agents), Blueprint (AI-assisted design). Mention it in interviews to show you're forward-looking. Target: All companies.

Defer — unless targeting CDH roles specifically

CPDC certification / CDH / NBA: This is a different specialization from case management. CBA, NAB, HSBC, SCB have CDH teams, but they hire CPDC-certified specialists. Only pursue this if you want to shift to decisioning/marketing — it's a career pivot, not a natural extension of your current profile.

The bottom line: Your fastest path into these companies is through CSFS/Collections + Integration + Constellation awareness. Your Mercedes-Benz Financial collections experience is a direct domain match for John Deere, Goldman Sachs, and Siemens CCMT. Your integration skills (Kafka, REST, SQL, file listeners) match what CBA, Cisco, Ford, and Sun Life are explicitly hiring for. Add basic Constellation UI knowledge and Smart Investigate/Dispute vocabulary to differentiate yourself from the typical "I'm a CSSA looking for a role" applicant. The companies that posted hiring for 4-7 years experience (VOIS, CBA, Lloyds, Sun Life, Broadridge) are your immediate targets.

Historical profile-date sample — not a hiring calendar

Archived September 2026 extraction from dated “from/since Month Year” text across audited profiles, movement radar and backfill tables. Dates can mark promotions, transfers or starts at non-Bengaluru teams, and the non-random ~330-profile sample is not a market-wide hiring census. Do not infer future vacancies or resignation timing from these bars. The newer Top 50 profile-start audit is kept separately in reports/bengaluru_join_timing_2026-11.json.

Largest observed bar: July (27 of 208 dated observations). June–September accounts for 91 of 208 (~44%), and January has 18. This is a distribution of extracted profile dates, not confirmed hires or a repeatable seasonal pattern.

Why this pattern, and what it means with a notice period

  • These are profile dates, not offer dates. Notice periods, start dates and approval cycles vary by employer and role; this sample cannot establish when an interview or offer occurred.
  • Month-of-year peaks are not a company hiring calendar. No employer-wide headcount or requisition data was used to validate the suggested budget-cycle explanations.
  • Some “since Month Year” mentions are internal promotions or title changes, not external hires — this inflates the count and is not separable with certainty from indexed text alone.
  • Sample bias: ~330 profiles chosen because they were already in your directory or came up during this audit, skewed to Bengaluru/Hyderabad BFSI/GCC Pega roles. It is not a random or complete market sample.

For your notice period specifically

Use a current employer requisition and your own contractual notice period to plan applications. Do not resign or predict an offer month based on these historical profile-date counts.

Departure-month mentions (2024–2026, n=21 — too small to trust on its own)

LWD/“left”/“ended” mentions cluster in June (5) with smaller counts in March, April, May, July and October (2 each); February and September had none in this sample. This is consistent with people serving notice after Q1 appraisal decisions and leaving before the next cycle, but 21 data points is not enough to be confident — it is shown for context, not as a rule.

Method: regex-mined from pega_full_audit.json findings and the HTML text of the movement radar/backfill/contact sections, deduplicated by month+year+context. Script: extract_dates.mjs → dates_extracted.json → aggregate_dates.mjs → date_histograms.json (kept alongside this file for reproducibility). All-time distribution (402 mentions, 2018–2026) shows the same July peak, so this is not purely a recent-window artifact.

Resume-fit reality check · why matches may not be converting

Checked 22 September 2026 against the actual PDF resume on file (Sathvik DN - Resume.pdf), not against the market-story framing built earlier in this hub.

The resume and the hub's own pitch don't match

The résumé says: Pega Developer, ~3.5–4 years, Mercedes-Benz R&D, CSSA + CSA. It quantifies: 80% manual-effort cut on CMS writeback, SMS cost to zero, ~£20K/year saved by decommissioning servers, 100+ case/flow changes, 20+ deployments at 99% success, zero-defect SFTP go-live.

The hub's "market story" card instead advertises $250K+ annual savings, a 25-hour batch moved to real-time, a 4-week task cut to 10 minutes, and L2/L3 incident ownership — none of which appear anywhere in the actual resume file. If those numbers are real, they need to be on the resume and LinkedIn, because ATS keyword screens and recruiters only ever see the document you submit, not this hub. If they're aspirational rather than verified, they should not be used in interviews as if they were resume-backed facts.

Likely seniority overreach

The resume shows a single employer, one non-senior title ("Pega Developer"), and no mention of Constellation, CDH/decisioning, cloud (AWS/Azure) or production on-call ownership. Several targets this hub has pushed — Booking SSA (5+ years), Standard Chartered/CBA decisioning-engineer routes, "CDH / Decisioning Engineer" and "AI Solutions Engineer" in the market-story role list — sit a level or a specialization above what the resume can currently defend. Applying there with this resume is a plausible reason for low conversion, independent of market conditions.

Corrected shortlist — matched to the resume as written, not the aspirational pitch

Same seniority band as your actual title (Pega Developer / Senior Software Engineer, 2–5 yrs), same stack (Kafka, REST/Connect, SFTP, case management), same domain where possible (auto finance / collections / BFSI integration). Pulled from the 329-record audit, not re-verified live.

How to use this table: lead with the résumé exactly as written — Kafka migration co-lead, CMS writeback REST integration, AXWAY SFTP framework, 20+ deployments, 99% success rate — and only bring in the bigger unwritten numbers if you can show your own evidence for them in the interview. Update the PDF resume itself before your next round of applications if those figures are real; a hub-only narrative that the submitted resume can't back up is the most fixable reason applications stall.

Your market story

Position yourself as a Pega integration and workflow engineer with real APAC collections delivery—not as a generic low-code configurator or an unproven AI-platform specialist.

Recommended headline

Pega CSSA · Kafka / REST / SFTP Integrations · SQL · Auto Finance & Collections · Case Management · Release Ownership

Scale50+ Kafka topics mapped into Pega staging tables across seven APAC markets.
Delivery100+ case and flow changes delivered across multiple releases.
IntegrationCMS writeback via REST API cut manual effort by about 80%.
CostReusable in-house SMS framework replaced four vendors and reduced SMS cost to zero.
OperationsAXWAY SFTP ingestion framework went live with zero defects; 20+ deployments at 99% success.
SavingsServer decommissioning saved roughly £20K per year.

Best role families

  1. Pega Integration or Platform Engineer
  2. Pega Developer / Senior Software Engineer
  3. Workflow Modernization Engineer
  4. BFSI / Collections Case-Management Engineer
  5. Developer Productivity / Internal Tools Engineer
  6. AI-assisted Automation Engineer, only where the role accepts learning-stage AI experience

Transition thesis

Your strongest near-term switch is Pega plus integration reliability. AI-assisted automation is a useful differentiator, but should support—not replace—the resume-backed Kafka, REST, SQL, SFTP and collections story.

Compensation framework

Company ranges are directional. Compare fixed, variable, employer contributions, joining bonus and equity separately.

₹27–28LOpening expectation
₹24–27LGood closing range
₹22–24LPreferred fixed
₹30–35L+Premium product stretch

TCS fallback · reconfirm

The earlier plan recorded ₹17L CTC. Its validity, project and joining date have not been rechecked for 22 September. Confirm the written offer and your current obligations before treating it as a fallback.

Avoid fake ₹24L

₹18–19L fixed plus uncertain variable, one-time bonus and employer contributions is not equivalent to ₹24L recurring fixed pay.

Your priorities · 30 September 2026

Keep your CSSA + Kafka/API/SFTP + collections experience at the centre. Separate employer fit from vacancy availability: one newly checked Citi role is the strongest current role-level lead, while most other recommendations still require a current role ID.

Expanded research: revised employer/contact priorities · verified recruiter leads · Full directory evidence audit · corrections and coverage limits.

Remote / hybrid · confirm the contractual work location

Reviewed 22 September 2026. A hybrid role in another city does not establish permission to work from Bengaluru.

Ask the recruiter for the base office, mandatory days per week, relocation requirements and any written remote-work exception. “PAN India” may describe recruitment coverage rather than permanent remote work. The previous 70%+ remote/hybrid claim had no reproducible source and is withdrawn.

Many internal Pega teams have no current job title or official customer story. Current employee clusters expose companies such as FNF India, Broadridge, Tesco and domestic banks that job-first searches miss.

What reverse search cannot prove

A profile cluster proves an internal talent footprint, not an open role, exact project, reporting chain or total team size. The profile must say current Pega work; old certifications and client assignments remain excluded.

Rejected or unsupported product-company claims

These companies were tested and should not be represented as India Pega employers without new primary evidence.

No defensible India Pega evidence

Qualcomm, Airtel, Lowe’s, JLR, BMW TechWorks, VW Digital Solutions, Volvo Cars, GE Aerospace, GE Vernova, BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, SLB, Boeing, Rolls-Royce, ABB, Eaton, CNH, Komatsu, Carrier and JCI. Career-adjacency false positives

Former Pegasystems employees, Pega certifications, “liked” posts, network-rule references, or generic automation work do not prove the current employer uses Pega.

Duplicate corporate groups

Credit Suisse is now counted under UBS. Express Scripts is covered by Evernorth/Cigna. DHL Supply Chain is not a separate row from DHL Group without distinct team evidence.

About awards

A company-level award proves strong implementation value, but not that every internal team or vacancy participated. Team-level awards are strongest where the exact COE/product is named, such as Stellantis Skill Currency or enGen Innovation.

About travel

Global products and PegaWorld speakers prove international collaboration and selective travel. They do not prove routine onsite opportunities. Ask for travel/rotation policy directly.

First message

Choose one current engineer whose experience resembles yours. Ask about the team and requisition route—not for an immediate referral.

Approach the architect or platform lead with a focused question about Kafka, Constellation, CDH, collections or production ownership.

Contact TA only with a live job ID, or ask whether they can route you to the recruiter who owns Pega hiring.

OLD BACKFILL ACTION PLAN WITHDRAWN · 22 SEPTEMBER 2026
The previous top-ten list converted departures, seniority changes and incomplete profile samples into guaranteed vacancies and attrition percentages. That inference is not reliable. The original wording remains in the untouched backup.

Use the revised outreach plan: verify the current role ID, legal employer, experience band and office policy. For Wells Fargo use relevant technical contacts rather than executive departures; for Optum use Pega-specific team evidence rather than the two rejected backfill examples. No net team-growth or attrition rate has been measured by this audit.

Outreach system

Do not message everyone at once. Use the employee who resembles your role first, then the architect/platform lead, then TA after locating a requisition.

Referral peer

Hi [Name], I’m a Pega CSSA with four years at MBRDI across Kafka, REST/SQL, auto-finance collections and L2/L3 production ownership. Your Pega work at [Company] looks closely aligned, and I’d value connecting and learning about the team.

Platform leader

Hi [Name], I’m a Pega CSSA at MBRDI with four years in Kafka integrations, collections and production automation. Your work leading [platform/team] matches the direction I’m pursuing. I’d value connecting and learning what capabilities your team prioritizes.

Recruiter with role ID

Hi [Name], I’ve applied for [title, requisition]. I’m a Pega CSSA with four years at MBRDI across Kafka, REST/SOAP, SQL, auto-finance collections and production automation. Could you advise whether my profile aligns with the approved level?

Follow-up

Thanks for connecting. I own Pega/Kafka modernization across seven APAC markets and built AI-assisted tooling that reduced mapping effort from four weeks to ten minutes. If your team has a suitable 4–6-year opening, would you be comfortable sharing the requisition or referral route?

Renewed 90-day campaign · 22 September–20 December 2026

A fresh planning window, not an assumption that your existing job search or offer timeline restarted. Adjust around your actual notice period and joining obligations.

22 Sep–5 Oct · Validate and activate

  • Confirm current notice period, offers and joining dates; the old TCS fallback is not assumed valid.
  • Recheck Citi 26985252 and Optum 2385172 on official portals.
  • Request suitable Bengaluru requisitions from five targeted peers.
  • Prepare six evidence-backed impact stories and a sanitized integration example.

6 Oct–5 Nov · Build interview momentum

  • Track application date, role ID, response and next action weekly.
  • Practice Constellation, APIs, security and Pega debugging.
  • Demonstrate Kafka retries, DLQ and idempotency.
  • Build a small tested AI automation example with human review and no employer data.

6 Nov–20 Dec · Compare and close

  • Maintain parallel interview conversations where feasible.
  • Compare recurring fixed pay separately from bonuses and equity.
  • Verify direct payroll, product ownership and office policy.
  • Decide against your actual joining deadlines, not an assumed old offer.

Evidence and maintenance rules

This is a living research snapshot, not a mathematically complete customer registry. Pega does not publicly disclose every customer, and many customer stories are anonymized.

Classification logic

  • Confirmed direct: named Pega use plus local direct team/hiring evidence.
  • Probable: strong signal, but one local ownership detail remains unresolved.
  • Global-only: company uses Pega, but India Pega ownership is unproven.
  • Rejected: certification, former employment, partner delivery or generic automation only.

Before acting

  • Recheck the current job and profile date.
  • Confirm legal employer and permanent/C2H status.
  • Ask which Pega product and version.
  • Confirm India owns architecture and roadmap.
  • Separate fixed, variable, equity and one-time pay.

Accuracy and privacy

Public contacts are professional profiles only. A manager title does not prove ownership of a vacancy. Never infer email addresses, disclose private data or upload MBRDI code/logs to public systems.
